{
  "hook": "At 1,300 meters in Tupungato's Serbal vineyard, Atamisque Chardonnay draws green apple snap and flinty minerality from nightly Andean chills that preserve acidity. Those altitude-driven temperature swings—days hitting 25°C, nights dropping to 10°C—build tension without tropical ripeness. Gold medals across vintages confirm its track record.",
  "wine_summary": "Atamisque crafts this Chardonnay from organic high-altitude sites in Valle de Tupungato, where the Uco Valley's elevation tempers Mendoza's heat for whites with backbone. The producer's focus on minimal intervention lets the site's alluvial soils and diurnal shifts dictate a profile of citrus peel and wet stone over oak-driven butter. This stands out in Argentina's white scene, where many chase ripeness but Atamisque prioritizes freshness amid rising demand for cool-climate values.",
  "terroir_expression": "Tupungato's gravelly alluvial soils, washed down from Andean volcanoes, drain fast and reflect heat, yielding concentrated berries with chalky undertones that translate to saline minerality in the glass. Cool climate from 1,300-meter elevation creates 15°C diurnal shifts, locking in malic acidity for green apple bite and piercing length. Quartz and limestone fragments add a smoky edge, distinct from warmer Mendoza valleys' softer peach profiles.",
  "vinification_summary": "Hand-harvested grapes ferment in stainless steel at cool temperatures to capture primary fruit without oxidation, skipping malolactic fermentation—which converts sharp malic acid to creamy lactic—to retain zesty acidity. Partial lees stirring builds texture without oak influence, emphasizing terroir over wood. This approach keeps alcohol balanced around 13% and delivers purity across vintages like the medal-winning 2018 and 2017.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken: acidity slices through fried spice and vinegar tang. Grilled sardines with lemon: mineral salinity echoes fish brine while cutting oiliness. Veal piccata: bright citrus matches caper acidity, with body holding against butter sauce. Bibb lettuce salad with goat cheese and walnuts: flinty notes amplify creamy tang and nutty crunch. Lobster thermidor: structure balances rich seafood without overwhelming delicacy.",
  "comparable_wines": "Salentein Barrel Selection Chardonnay — shares Tupungato altitude for similar apple-mineral drive, but adds subtle oak. Doña Paula Estate Chardonnay — Uco Valley peer with gravel soils yielding crisp acidity, less flinty.",
  "style_profile": "Medium-bodied dry white with high acidity and flinty minerality",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink within 3-5 years of vintage for peak freshness. Store at 55°F away from light to hold acidity.",
  "value_assessment": "$18-25 retail. Stacks up to Catena White Bones Chardonnay or O. Fournier Urban Uco at the same price—fresher site expression without blending tricks. Buy it for consistent quality that punches above entry-level Argentines.",
  "market_position": "Sommeliers list it for by-the-glass whites in casual bistros from Buenos Aires to Brooklyn. Retail shelves target value seekers upgrading from Sauvignon Blanc. Not a collector's pick, but steady for everyday sipping.",
  "insider_take": "Skip this if you demand overt oak butter—its restraint frustrates New World Chardonnay fans. Tradeoff is purity over plushness, ideal for acidity junkies tired of flabby alternatives. Atamisque nails the high-altitude template better than most Tupungato rivals.",

parsed.hook: At 1,300 meters in Tupungato's Serbal vineyard, Atamisque Chardonnay draws green apple snap and flinty minerality from nightly Andean chills that preserve acidity. Those altitude-driven temperature swings—days hitting 25°C, nights dropping to 10°C—build tension without tropical ripeness. Gold medals across vintages confirm its track record.
parsed.wine_summary: Atamisque crafts this Chardonnay from organic high-altitude sites in Valle de Tupungato, where the Uco Valley's elevation tempers Mendoza's heat for whites with backbone. The producer's focus on minimal intervention lets the site's alluvial soils and diurnal shifts dictate a profile of citrus peel and wet stone over oak-driven butter. This stands out in Argentina's white scene, where many chase ripeness but Atamisque prioritizes freshness amid rising demand for cool-climate values.
parsed.terroir_expression: Tupungato's gravelly alluvial soils, washed down from Andean volcanoes, drain fast and reflect heat, yielding concentrated berries with chalky undertones that translate to saline minerality in the glass. Cool climate from 1,300-meter elevation creates 15°C diurnal shifts, locking in malic acidity for green apple bite and piercing length. Quartz and limestone fragments add a smoky edge, distinct from warmer Mendoza valleys' softer peach profiles.
parsed.vinification_summary: Hand-harvested grapes ferment in stainless steel at cool temperatures to capture primary fruit without oxidation, skipping malolactic fermentation—which converts sharp malic acid to creamy lactic—to retain zesty acidity. Partial lees stirring builds texture without oak influence, emphasizing terroir over wood. This approach keeps alcohol balanced around 13% and delivers purity across vintages like the medal-winning 2018 and 2017.

Lobster thermidor: structure balances rich seafood without overwhelming delicacy.

parsed.value_assessment: $18-25 retail. Stacks up to Catena White Bones Chardonnay or O. Fournier Urban Uco at the same price—fresher site expression without blending tricks. Buy it for consistent quality that punches above entry-level Argentines.
